questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=-2{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-3{b}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =5{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\  & =-2{b}_{2}+5{b}_{1} \\  & =-2{b}_{2}-\frac{5}{3}(-3{b}_{1}) \\  & ={c}_{1}-\frac{5}{3}{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. By adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=2{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}={b}_{1}+(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =7{b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\  & =7(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})+(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}) \\  & =\frac{7}{2}{c}_{1}-\frac{7}{2}{c}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2} \\  & =4{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=4{b}_{3}$, ${c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}$ and ${c}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}+8{b}_{3} \\  & =8{b}_{3}+2{b}_{1}+2{b}_{2} \\  & =2(4{b}_{3})+2{b}_{1}+2\cdot 2(\frac{1}{2}{b}_{2}) \\  & =2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}+4{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}+3{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Multiplying the second equation by $-2$ and adding the equations, we get  

$$
{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}=-{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{c}_{2}={b}_{1}+2(-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2})\,⟹\,{b}_{1}=2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =2(2{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2})-3(-{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2}+3{c}_{1}-6{c}_{2} \\  & =7{c}_{1}-12{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -12\end{aligned}].$
